title: "Are AI Systems About to Start Building Themselves?"
description: "Jack Clark's essay arguing the public technical evidence on coding, kernel design, fine-tuning, and AI-system management points to a roughly 60% chance of fully automated AI R&D by the end of 2028."
author: synesis
date: "2026-05-08"

![Image from [Import AI](https://importai.substack.com/).](cover.jpg){fig-align="center"}

[Jack Clark](https://jack-clark.net/), co-founder and policy lead at Anthropic, [walks through](https://importai.substack.com/p/import-ai-455-automating-ai-research) the public evidence that automated AI research and development (R&D), a frontier model autonomously training its own successor, has a roughly 60% chance of arriving by the end of 2028, and a 30% chance by 2027. The essay collects benchmark trends across coding, scientific reproduction, kernel design, fine-tuning, alignment-research automation, and time-horizon scaling, then argues each of those covers a distinct ingredient of the AI-engineering pipeline.

What Clark argues:

- **Coding and time horizon are the foundation.** SWE-Bench [[1]](#ref-1) went from ~2% (Claude 2, late 2023) to 93.9% (Claude Mythos Preview), and the [Model Evaluation and Threat Research (METR)](https://metr.org/) 50%-reliability time horizon [[2]](#ref-2) went from ~30 seconds (GPT-3.5, 2022) to ~12 hours (Opus 4.6, 2026), with [Ajeya Cotra](https://www.openphilanthropy.org/about/team/ajeya-cotra/) (AI forecaster at METR) expecting ~100 hours by the end of 2026. Long horizons are what let an agent run a day's worth of researcher work without re-calibration.

- **Every sub-skill of the AI-R&D pipeline has a trending benchmark.** Paper reproduction (CORE-Bench [[3]](#ref-3)) went from 21.5% (GPT-4o, Sept 2024) to 95.5% declared solved (Opus 4.5, Dec 2025). Kaggle-style ML engineering (MLE-Bench [[4]](#ref-4)) went from 16.9% (o1, Oct 2024) to 64.4% (Gemini 3 with search, Feb 2026). On PostTrainBench [[5]](#ref-5), Opus 4.6 and GPT-5.4 get 25–28% against a human-instruct-tuned baseline of 51%. GPU kernel design has several active research lines (DeepSeek kernels, Meta Triton automation, Huawei Ascend, CUDA Agent fine-tuning), though Clark notes kernels benefit from easily verifiable rewards. And Anthropic's Automated Alignment Research proof-of-concept has AI agents beating a human baseline on scalable oversight at small scale.

- **Training-loop optimization is the cleanest single trend.** On Anthropic's internal CPU-only language-model training task [[6]](#ref-6), speedup went from 2.9x (Opus 4, May 2025) to 16.5x (Opus 4.5, Nov 2025) to 30x (Opus 4.6, Feb 2026) to 52x (Mythos Preview, Apr 2026), against a human baseline of 4x in 4–8 hours.

- **Management is a meta-skill.** Claude Code and OpenCode already show a single agent supervising sub-agents, forming synthetic teams with directors, critics, and engineers that can fan out across a complex project.

- **Creativity is why 2027 sits at 30% rather than 60%.** Clark argues AI research is mostly Edison's 99% perspiration, the engineering schlep the benchmarks above already cover, but paradigm shifts like the transformer or mixture-of-experts still come from humans. Preliminary creativity signs (a Gemini model resolving Erdős-1051 [[7]](#ref-7); a UBC / UNSW / Stanford / Google DeepMind centaur math proof [[8]](#ref-8)) cluster in math and CS and may not generalize. The 2027 gap is his estimate of how often a year-scale human insight is still required. If no proof-of-concept lands by end of 2028, he treats that as evidence the current paradigm has a fundamental gap.

- **Industry intent as corroboration.** OpenAI targets an "automated AI research intern by September 2026" [[9]](#ref-9); Anthropic publishes automated alignment research [[10]](#ref-10); DeepMind endorses alignment automation "when feasible" [[11]](#ref-11); Recursive Superintelligence raised $500M for AI-R&D automation [[12]](#ref-12) and Mirendil [[13]](#ref-13) targets the same. Hundreds of billions of capital is aimed at this outcome.

## My Notes

- None of these benchmarks individually proves recursive self-improvement, but together they describe a system that can do most of the engineering schlep without supervision.

- Clark puts 30% on automated AI R&D by 2027 and 60% by 2028. The gap is a bet that some research insights still come from humans on a year-or-more cadence. The creativity window is on the order of a year.

- The Aletheia/Erdős-problems pipeline [[7]](#ref-7) evaluated around 700 conjectures and produced 13 addressable problems — 5 novel autonomous solutions plus 8 that turned out to match existing literature — with 1 deemed genuinely interesting. A funnel dominated by human filtering. That fits [Terence Tao](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Terence_Tao)'s [generation / verification / digestion decomposition](/posts/20260422-proof-generation-vs-digestion/): AI is strong on the first two, and the research taste stays with the humans doing digestion. Clark describes this as a "centaur configuration": humans collaborating with AI rather than AI acting alone. The pattern is real, but human mathematicians are still the scarce input.

- On Anthropic's CPU-only training-optimization benchmark, the 2.9x → 52x speedup chain hasn't flattened, and the human 4x baseline was passed three generations ago. Another year at this pace would make the 30%-by-2027 probability look too conservative.

- The alignment section is brief, but the compounding-error math Clark cites (99.9% accuracy → 95.12% after 50 generations → 60.5% after 500) is the quantitative reason getting alignment right before recursion starts matters more than fixing it along the way. The math assumes per-generation drift compounds independently, which is generous — if drift correlates across generations the curve steepens fast.

- [ARC-AGI-3](/posts/20260506-arc-agi-3-failure-modes/) is a live test of both the creativity gap and the drift math. GPT-5.5 scored 0.43% and Opus 4.7 scored 0.18% on a benchmark that withholds instructions and forces models to infer rules from sparse feedback. Clark's benchmarks are mostly in-distribution with verifiable rewards, which is where current models climb fastest. Two of the three failure modes pulled from the reasoning traces pick up his caveats directly. Failure 2 (reusing a Tetris or Sokoban template for unfamiliar mechanics) is what happens when a system hits a genuinely novel direction with no training match. Failure 3 (reward cementing the wrong primitive after a lucky level-beat) is the empirical shape of the compounding-drift math. If AI R&D includes material amounts of either, Clark's estimate looks too optimistic.

- The economic bullets are weaker than the technical ones, partly because the labor data through today still sits where the rebuttal in [The 2028 Global Intelligence Crisis](/posts/20260502-2028-intelligence-crisis/) described it: low-4s unemployment, rising new-business formation, software-engineer postings up year-over-year. The essay does not attempt to reconcile a 2028 R&D-automation forecast with a 2026 labor market that is not yet inflecting.
